title: Amazon to invest $7 billion in Indian renewable energy by 2030, adds 934 MW of wind and solar projects
excerpt: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, on top of the $4 billion it has already contracted in the country, the company said. Alongside the commitment, the company announced four new utility-scale wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts (MW). The company said in a statement that the plan makes it one of India's leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy. Taken together, Amazon's contracted and planned spending on clean power in India now comes to $11 billion. The four new projects The largest of the four is a 234 MW wind farm in Bijapur, Karnataka, which Amazon said is its largest contracted wind project in Asia to date. The others are a 200 MW combined solar and wind project in Tumkur, Karnataka, a 300 MW solar project in Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh, and a 200 MW solar project in Dinkar, Rajasthan. The projects have been secured through power purchase agreements (PPAs) with renewable energy developers Waaree, ReNew and Sunsure. Sunsure is developing both Karnataka projects, Waaree the Madhya Pradesh project and ReNew the Rajasthan project, according to pv magazine India. The four projects fall under the $4 billion that Amazon has already contracted, not the new $7 billion. Once operational, Amazon's contracted renewable energy projects in India will have a combined capacity of more than 2 gigawatts (GW). The company said they will generate electricity equivalent to the annual needs of more than 3.5 million Indian households. What the minister and Amazon said “We welcome Amazon's continued investment in renewable energy in India. Such investments play an important role in advancing India's clean energy ambitions, strengthening energy security and supporting sustainable economic growth,” Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said. “They also demonstrate the growing confidence of global companies in India's renewable energy sector and its potential to attract long-term investment, create economic opportunities and accelerate the country's energy transition,” he added. Kara Hurst, Chief Sustainability Officer at Amazon, said, “This additional investment of $7 billion underlines our long-term commitment, helping bring additional wind and solar capacity online while contributing to India's energy security and long-term renewable energy ambitions.” “By expanding access to renewable energy at scale, we aim to help meet India's growing electricity demand, strengthen the country's energy security and contribute to its ambitious goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070,” she said. A new global carbon target Amazon said the India investments will contribute to its new global goal of reducing the carbon intensity of the electricity powering its operations by 65% by 2030, compared with a 2019 baseline. In practice, this means every unit of electricity the company consumes would be associated with 65% fewer carbon emissions than in 2019. The target sits under The Climate Pledge, Amazon's commitment to reach net-zero carbon emissions across its operations by 2040. Globally, Amazon has more than 700 wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of over 40 GW. How Amazon's India portfolio has grown Amazon's renewable energy push in India began in September 2022, when it announced its first three solar farms in Rajasthan with a combined capacity of 420 MW. ReNew Power was behind 210 MW of that, with Amp Energy India and Brookfield Renewable accounting for the rest. In February 2025, the company added three wind farms totalling 379 MW in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, developed by CleanMax, BluPine and JSW Energy. At that point it counted 53 projects in India, including nine utility-scale projects and 44 on-site solar arrays, and said they could power over 1.3 million Indian homes a year. The portfolio now stands at 57 projects: 14 utility-scale wind and solar projects that supply power to the grid and 43 on-site solar installations at its facilities. The number of utility-scale projects has risen from nine to 14 in under two years, and the household-equivalent figure has grown from 1.3 million to more than 3.5 million. Part of a larger India commitment The renewable energy plan adds to Amazon's other large investment pledges for India. In 2025, the company said it would invest $35 billion across all its businesses in the country by 2030. In June this year, after CEO Andy Jassy met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, Amazon announced a further $13 billion for AI and cloud infrastructure, taking its planned investment in India for 2026-2030 to $48 billion. That money is meant to expand AWS data centre capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad. Beyond electricity The company also gave updates on its other sustainability efforts in India. It has deployed more than 15,000 electric vehicles (EV) across over 500 cities and is working with Tata Motors to deploy 3,000 electric trucks. It also plans 1,000 more electric trucks for its Amazon Now operations. Amazon said it became water-positive in India in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target, returning more than 120% of the water used directly in its operations. It has invested more than Rs 62 crore in water replenishment projects, which are expected to replenish over 4 billion litres of water a year. More than 50% of customer orders in India are now shipped in reduced or original packaging, and the company is working with IIT Roorkee to develop alternative packaging materials from agricultural residue. The announcement comes as India's own capacity build-out gathers pace. According to government data released last week, India's installed power capacity stood at about 560 GW in October 2026, with non-fossil sources accounting for 55%. Solar capacity reached nearly 175 GW by 31 October, up from 2.8 GW in 2014.

title: Atain Appoints Jitendra Sindhwani (Jimpy) as Chief Executive Officer
excerpt: WASHINGTON and GURGAON, India, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Atain, an enterprise orchestration partner that aligns people, processes, and platforms with AI to deliver assured outcomes, announced the appointment of Jitendra Sindhwani (Jimpy) as Chief Executive Officer, effective November 16, 2026. Jitendra Sindhwani Jimpy is a seasoned technology and business leader with over three decades of experience across IT services and enterprise software. He has led large global teams and organizations across go-to-market, product, and delivery functions, built and launched new businesses, and helped drive transformation across industries. Most recently at IBS Software, a leading SaaS provider to the global travel industry, he held senior leadership roles spanning global revenue growth, business operations, product innovation, and transformation. For over a decade, he has helped scale the travel, logistics, and hospitality businesses, launched cutting-edge technology platforms, and built strategic partnerships with global travel enterprises. Prior to IBS Software, Jimpy spent 16 years at Infosys, leading global businesses across telecommunications, media, and entertainment, and delivering end-to-end technology solutions, including IT and customer experience services. Jimpy will lead Atain's next phase of growth, building on its domain expertise and customer relationships through AI-led innovation. "On behalf of the entire company and the Board of Directors, I am delighted to welcome Jimpy to Atain," said John Del Santo, Chair of the Atain Board. "He brings a proven track record of client partnership and commercial leadership across industries. Jimpy has the vision and experience to take Atain through its next phase of growth, and we look forward to working with him." On joining Atain, Jimpy said: "I am excited to join Atain at an inflection point in its journey, with deep domain expertise, strong customer relationships, and an organization that people want to be part of. As AI reshapes how enterprises operate, I look forward to working with our people, customers, and partners to shape what comes next." Jimpy holds an engineering degree from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a postgraduate in management from the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bangalore. He is based in Washington, D.C., USA. About Atain Atain is an enterprise orchestration partner that brings together people, processes, platforms, and AI to deliver assured business outcomes. Combining deep domain expertise with technology-led innovation, Atain helps global enterprises transform operations, enhance customer experiences, and drive sustainable growth.

title: Maha announces India's first sulfur dioxide emissions market to tackle industrial pollution
excerpt: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) announced India's first sulfur dioxide pollution market on Tuesday, aiming to improve air quality and support economic growth. The announcement was made during an event attended by the state's Minister for Environment and Climate Change.â€‹Under the new statewide Maharashtra Sulfur Dioxide Emissions Trading Scheme, approximately 130 million residents are expected to benefit from improved air quality.â€‹The market is designed to control pollution by enabling participating plants to trade emission permits. This mechanism incentivises industrial plants with lower pollution-reduction costs to make substantial cuts and sell excess permits to facilities facing higher compliance costs. The pilot launch follows years of preparation by regulatory authorities to establish accurate emissions tracking mechanisms. The initiative is being executed in close collaboration with academic and research partners to scale emissions trading across the region.â€‹Addressing the gathering, the Environment Minister emphasised the need to leverage technology, including artificial intelligence, to monitor industrial pollution intelligently and foster collaborative solutions. Officials reiterated that the regulatory approach focuses on cooperating with industries to foster sustainable development alongside environmental protection. title: Maha announces India’s first sulfur dioxide emissions market to tackle industrial pollution
excerpt: Mumbai, Nov 17 (IANS) The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) announced India's first sulfur dioxide pollution market on Tuesday, aiming to improve air quality and support economic growth. The announcement was made during an event attended by the state's Minister for Environment and Climate Change. Under the new statewide Maharashtra Sulfur Dioxide Emissions Trading Scheme, approximately 130 million residents are expected to benefit from improved air quality. The market is designed to control pollution by enabling participating plants to trade emission permits. This mechanism incentivises industrial plants with lower pollution-reduction costs to make substantial cuts and sell excess permits to facilities facing higher compliance costs. The pilot launch follows years of preparation by regulatory authorities to establish accurate emissions tracking mechanisms. The initiative is being executed in close collaboration with academic and research partners to scale emissions trading across the region. Custom Ad: Multiplex Addressing the gathering, the Environment Minister emphasised the need to leverage technology, including artificial intelligence, to monitor industrial pollution intelligently and foster collaborative solutions. Officials reiterated that the regulatory approach focuses on cooperating with industries to foster sustainable development alongside environmental protection. Furthermore, regulatory authorities and a prominent research institute signed a separate Memorandum of Understanding to advance data-driven environmental governance using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The partnership will jointly develop and pilot an AI-assisted inspection framework designed to help officials identify industrial facilities with a higher probability of non-compliance, supported by regular technical training and data analytics workshops for inspectors. --IANS sj/dan
